text:
leo tran: hi all, just started. i can reach internal services by IP but not by hostname (e.g., http://ci.internal.redwood). macbook air (Monterey). tried restarts, VPN shows connected. any quick tips?

marie k: welcome leo! usually this is split-tunnel DNS. do you see our internal resolver pushed? run `scutil --dns` and paste the resolver blocks.

leo tran: here's the snippet that looks suspicious:
```
resolver #2
  domain   : internal.redwood
  nameserver[0] : 8.8.8.8
```
so it's pointing at google.

raj p: that explains it. Corporate VPN should push 10.11.5.3 as the nameserver for internal.redwood. Are you on the wireguard-wrapper client or the built-in mac vpn?

leo tran: corporate wireguard client (installed by IT).

marie k: two things to try: 1) temporarily add /etc/resolver/internal.redwood with `nameserver 10.11.5.3` and 2) check chrome's secure DNS setting (chrome://settings/security) because DoH will bypass system resolver.

leo tran: added resolver file and still no luck in chrome. terminal `curl ci.internal.redwood` works after the file. chrome name lookup fails.

raj p: yep classic DoH clash. Toggle "Use secure DNS" off and retest. Also older macOS versions have race conditions where the resolver file isn't honored until you flush mDNSResponder: `sudo dscacheutil -flushcache; sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder`

leo tran: toggled DoH off, flushed cache, chrome is happy now. thanks!

infra-bot: VPN route confirmed: pushed DNS 10.11.5.3 for /internal.redwood via wg-gateway-2 at 2066004380.

marie k: i'll add a short note in the onboarding doc under "Networking" about Mac + DoH + split-tunnel and link to this thread.

raj p: followup action: infra will update the wireguard wrapper to write /etc/resolver entries on connect for macs and ensure the DNS push uses domain-scoped resolver, not global. tagging infra team to track.

leo tran: really appreciate the help, saved me a frantic 1st-day support ping :thumbsup:
